messages:
infra-bot: ALERT: Repeated health-check flaps detected for routing group 'smart-router:rdm-2.1' -> rapid failovers between regions (us-east <-> us-west <-> eu). Observed 3x fallback events in 6m. Probable cause: variant mismatch during fallback (rdm-2.1-int8 vs rdm-2.1-quant) + health probe validation failures. Severity P1. See: https://internal.redwood/ops/inc/1812345678

pagerduty-bot: Paging Ops Oncall (Maria G.). Incident assigned.

Maria G.: Oncall here. Investigating now. Which customers are affected and any recent deploys?

Alex T.: We did a canary of int8 variant in eu/us-west ~10m ago. Logs show probe responses from int8 are returning 200 but missing required validation header X-Model-Variant, router treats as unhealthy -> marks node down -> fallback to us-east which has quant variant. That triggers higher latency and load, then us-west recovers, repeat. Edge 502/504 spike correlates.

Tom H.: So it's a policy + probe mismatch. I can do a quick mitigation: pin affected traffic to us-east or disable cross-region auto-fallback for rdm-2.1. What's lowest-risk?

Lee R.: Low-risk steps: 1) disable auto-fallback on rdm-2.1 routing policy (prevents flipflop) 2) raise health-check threshold to 3 failures 3) clear prefix/KV caches for rdm-2.1 in us-west to avoid stale connections. I'll paste the patch.

Lee R.: ```bash
# pin routing and disable fallback for affected model group
curl -X PATCH https://admin.redwood/api/routing/policies/rdm-2.1 \n -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \n -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n -d '{"auto_fallback": false, "preferred_regions": ["us-east-1"], "health_threshold": 3}'
```

Jess C.: Noting impact: telemetry shows 12 tenant namespaces with degraded latency, 4 enterprise customers reporting 5xxs, and token latency doubled in fallback windows. I'll alert CS and start customer comms.

Samir P.: Maria, handing the mitigation to you. I'll stand by for verification.

Maria G.: Applying the routing patch now. Executing CLI...

Maria G.: Response: 200 OK. Policy updated. Monitoring metrics.

infra-bot: AUTO-DETECT: After policy update, fallback events rate decreased from 0.5/min to 0.05/min over 3m. Health probe failure rate in us-west dropped to baseline.

Alex T.: Still seeing a few timeouts — probably long-lived upstream connections. Suggest clearing router caches for that model in us-west.

Tom H.: Command to clear prefix cache: ```bash
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood/api/cache/clear \n -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \n -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n -d '{"model":"rdm-2.1","region":"us-west-2","scope":"prefix"}'
```

Maria G.: Cache clear issued. Router logs (excerpt): ```json
{"ts":"2026-03-15T17:22:03Z","route":"rdm-2.1","event":"fallback","from":"us-west-2","to":"us-east-1","reason":"probe_header_missing","probe_fail_count":2}
```

Maria G.: After cache clear + policy patch, 5xxs dropped ~80% in affected tenants. Latency trending back to normal. Keeping monitoring for 30m.

Jess C.: CS ping sent to the 4 customers. Notified them it's a routing fallback issue, mitigation applied, postmortem to follow.

Samir P.: Postmortem owners: Tom H. (root cause analysis), Lee R. (mitigation timeline & config), Jess C. (customer comms).

Maria G.: Handoff to next oncall (Lee R.) at 18:00 UTC. Leaving notes in the incident runbook channel.

Ops Oncall: Acknowledged. Incident moved to monitoring. Will escalate if flakes reappear (>2 flaps in 10m).

Jess C.: Quick action items for PM/Platform: 1) validate probe contract across all variants (header + schema) 2) add a canary check for routing-policy-change-to-avoid-variant-mismatch 3) tighten rollout guidance for quant vs int8.

Alex T.: I'll open a CL to add strict probe header validation and add an automated test in the model onboarding pipeline.

Maria G.: Thanks team. Closing active mitigation. Recording this thread to the incidents repo and creating a follow-up ticket for the postmortem.
